subject: Data lifecycle orchestration & subprocessor erase schedule (DPA implications)
messages:
From: Ellen Mueller <ellen.mueller@medisafe.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Medisafe Legal <legal@medisafe.com>
Date: 2025-10-12T09:14:00-04:00
Subject: Clarify: backup purge timing & log retention exception for audit evidence

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the demo last week — good to see how Redwood handles prefix caching and the routing policies. Before we move to procurement we need to lock down a couple of operational commitments that are DPA-critical for our compliance team. Two asks from Legal/Audit: 

1) Backup purge timeline: our auditors require an ability to retrieve user-level evidence up to 90 days after an event in certain regulated workflows. Can Redwood support a 90-day snapshot hold window followed by automatic purge? If not, what are the options for a temporary extension (restore-grace) and who can trigger it?

2) Log retention exception: Medisafe needs an exception to hold some anonymized audit logs up to 180 days for investigations. Access must be strictly controlled and appear in audit logs. Is Redwood able to provide a limited-access exception scoped by request and role?

Separately, the DPA needs an up-to-date subprocessor list and confirmation that EU data will not be routed through non-EU subprocessors without SCC or explicit consent. Please attach the latest subprocessors CSV and a draft DPA amendment if possible.

Appreciate a short timeline/next steps — our procurement would like to include any DPA redlines in the first DocuSign packet.

Thanks,
Ellen
Ellen Mueller
Head of IT Compliance | Medisafe Health
ellen.mueller@medisafe.com

--
Attachment: none

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Mueller <ellen.mueller@medisafe.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-12T11:02:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: backup purge timing & log retention exception for audit evidence

Hi Ellen — thanks for the clear ask and for surfacing the auditor requirements. Looping in Markus (legal) and Priyom (platform ops) to propose a concrete plan. High level responses below; I'll follow up with attachments and a proposed DPA amendment draft by EOD.

Backup purge window: we can support a 90-day snapshot hold as an option. Our usual platform default is 30-day snapshot retention for hosted accounts, but we have a configurable "restore-grace" policy that can be extended to 90 days for contracted customers. The extension is controlled by an ops ticket and requires approval from the customer admin + a legal authorization for DPA amendment.

Log retention exception: Platform can scope a limited-access log retention exception up to 180 days. We would implement this as a separate retention class ("audit-evidence") with role-based access controls and read-only retrieval via an audited export process. Priyom, can you confirm whether exports are pseudonymization-friendly for EU-only evidence?

Next steps (proposed):
- We will attach: current subprocessors list + retention matrix (backup_retention_matrix.xlsx).
- Markus will draft a short DPA amendment that includes both the 90-day snapshot hold and the 180-day log exception, with an approval workflow and a defined emergency restore process (DocuSign-ready).
- Timeline: draft to you by COB 2025-10-12; internal review and signoff by 2025-10-14; DocuSign go-live target 2025-10-16.

If you have a procurement gating milestone earlier than that, let me know and we'll accelerate.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

--
Attachment: backup_retention_matrix.xlsx (stub)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellen Mueller <ellen.mueller@medisafe.com>
Date: 2025-10-13T09:30:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: backup purge timing & log retention exception for audit evidence

Stephanie / Priyom / Ellen — quick legal + control note. I drafted the DPA amendment and included operational controls that map to Medisafe's asks. Key points: 

1) Snapshot purge and restore-grace
- We can contractually offer a 90-day snapshot retention class. After 90 days snapshots are purged automatically.
- We will include a one-time 30-day restore-grace extension that can only be triggered by an authorized Medisafe admin via our support portal; triggers must include requestor identity and business justification; all actions are logged.

2) Log retention exception
- Approve a scoped 180-day retention for "audit-evidence" logs. Access to these logs will be restricted to a named set of customer roles and require two-step approval for exports. Exports will be pseudonymized by default; full identifiers require an elevated legal request and RBAC justification.

3) Subprocessors and transfers
- Attached is the current subprocessors list (subprocessors_current_list.csv). For EU-region accounts we ensure primary storage and primary processing stay within EU regions; any cross-border processing uses SCCs and is listed in the amendment.

4) Controls and proof
- We will provide audit evidence (access logs) showing who exported or restored data and when. Redwood's console will retain token-level trace for 365 days for compliance review; however snapshot contents are purged per contractual retention.

5) Operational SLAs and signoff
- I recommend the following signoff path: Medisafe Legal signs the DPA amendment --> Redwood security verifies RBAC setup --> Redwood ops implements the retention class and test restore.

I've attached the draft amendment and subprocessors CSV for review. Stephanie, please send to Ellen and procurement; if they accept the language we'll spin a DocuSign envelope (link below) and plan a short test restore in staging.

Drafts attached: dpa_amendment_draft_v1.docx, subprocessors_current_list.csv

DocuSign placeholder: https://www.docusign.com/mt/DocuSignLinkPlaceholder

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Legal | Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Clarify: backup purge timing & log retention exception for audit evidence

Markus / Stephanie — thanks for the quick turnaround and for including the operational controls. Medisafe Legal has reviewed the draft amendment and is comfortable with the 90-day snapshot hold, the one-time 30-day restore-grace (admin-triggered), and a 180-day audit-evidence log retention with RBAC + export logging. A couple of minor asks before we sign: 

- Please add a short clause that any full-identifier export requires a documented legal justification and will be flagged to our security contact.
- Can you include a Confluence link with a short runbook for the test restore and the backstop timeline (we need to run a dry restore as part of our onboarding)?

If you add that clause and the runbook link we can proceed to DocuSign. Target: sign by 2025-10-16.
